questions.q: The correct decreasing order of acidity is:
questions.explain: Ortho and para nitro groups stabilise phenoxide by resonance, but in o-nitrophenol the OH proton is held by an intramolecular hydrogen bond, so para (7.1) edges out ortho (7.2); meta (8.3) acts only by −I.

questions.q: Which of the following is a weaker acid than phenol?
questions.explain: The methyl group releases electrons and destabilises the phenoxide ion, so p-cresol (pKa 10.2) is weaker than phenol (10.0). Chloro and nitro groups raise acidity.

questions.q: The correct order of acidity among the chlorophenols is:
questions.explain: For halophenols the −I effect wins and falls off with distance, and at para the +R donation partly cancels it: o (8.56) > m (9.12) > p (9.41).

questions.q: Arrange in increasing acidity: propan-1-ol (I), 4-methylphenol (II), phenol (III), 3-nitrophenol (IV), 3,5-dinitrophenol (V), 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (VI).
options: I < II < III < IV < V < VI
II < I < III < IV < V < VI
I < III < II < IV < V < VI
I < II < III < V < IV < VI
questions.explain: An alcohol is far weaker than any phenol; the methyl group weakens phenol; each nitro group strengthens it, with picric acid (pKa 0.38) strongest. The trap is placing 4-methylphenol above phenol.
